hints: State the principle of conservation of linear momentum: total initial momentum equals total final momentum.
Take the initial direction of motion of $P$ as positive, so $u_P = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $v_P = -0.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Form the equation $m(2) + 0.2(0) = m(-0.5) + 0.2(1)$ and solve for $m$.
walkthrough:
Apply conservation of linear momentum, taking the initial direction of $P$ as positive:
$$m_P u_P + m_Q u_Q = m_P v_P + m_Q v_Q$$

Substitute the given masses and velocities with $u_P = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $u_Q = 0$, $v_P = -0.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ (opposite direction), and $v_Q = 1\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$m(2) + 0.2(0) = m(-0.5) + 0.2(1)$$
$$2m = -0.5m + 0.2$$

ai_rubric.Conserving Linear Momentum: Applies $m(2) + 0 = m(-0.5) + 0.2(1)$ and solves to obtain $m = 0.08\text{ kg}$.

teacher_walkthrough:
State the principle of conservation of linear momentum for an isolated system in one dimension:
$$m_P u_P + m_Q u_Q = m_P v_P + m_Q v_Q$$
Choose a sign convention: let motion to the right (the initial direction of $P$) be positive.

List the known quantities:
Mass of $P = m\text{ kg}$, initial velocity $u_P = +2\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Mass of $Q = 0.2\text{ kg}$, initial velocity $u_Q = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
After impact, $P$ rebounds in the opposite direction: $v_P = -0.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
$Q$ moves in the initial direction of $P$: $v_Q = +1\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Substitute these values into the momentum conservation equation:
$$m(2) + 0.2(0) = m(-0.5) + 0.2(1)$$
$$2m = -0.5m + 0.2$$

Add $0.5m$ to both sides to collect like terms:
$$2.5m = 0.2$$
Divide both sides by $2.5$:
$$m = \frac{0.2}{2.5} = \frac{2}{25} = 0.08\text{ kg}$$
